title: Ledger and Lantern
premise: Juniper Dunmore, indentured to the Meridian Trading Company in the port city of Saltmere, has learned to keep their head down and believe history belongs to other people. When a stranger named Oren Voss arrives clutching letters in the unmistakable hand of Captain Elias Dunmore—Juniper's father, declared dead seven years ago—the two discover the letters prove the Company falsified shipwreck records to seize pearl-divers' estates. To deliver the ledger pages to a magistrate three checkpoints away before the Company's audit destroys them, Juniper and Oren must rely on a makeshift family of divers, scribes, and smugglers. In the end, Juniper testifies as the last living Dunmore, choosing inheritance not of property but of memory—and the found family that carries it.
about_author: Mirabel Joubert is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal cottage, where she collects tide charts and unanswered letters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. We meet them scrubbing the Company's countinghouse floors, tallying debts they'll never escape, convinced their father drowned and their history ended with him. A quiet chapter establishing the numbness of indenture. Emotional beat: resignation mistaken for peace, cracked slightly when Juniper finds their own name misfiled under 'deceased.'

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Ink
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Oren Voss arrives at the countinghouse, half-drowned and hunted, carrying letters in Elias Dunmore's handwriting—dated after the shipwreck. Juniper recognizes the loops of their father's hand and cannot breathe. Emotional beat: shock and denial, the first tremor of hope in seven years, and the immediate danger Oren's arrival brings to both.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Swallowed
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. In a diver's cellar, Oren explains: he served under Captain Dunmore, who survived the wreck and spent years gathering proof that the Company sank its own ships to claim estates. The letters point to a hidden ledger. Emotional beat: Oren's guilt over failing the captain, transferred into fierce protectiveness of his child.

chapters.title: The Divers' Table
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper is taken to a hidden supper among pearl divers—people who knew their father, who argue and sing and claim them without ceremony. For the first time, history feels like something they belong to. Emotional beat: the aching warmth of found family, shadowed by the news that the Company's audit begins in nine days.

chapters.title: Nine Days to Saltmere Gate
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. The plan forms: the ledger pages must reach Magistrate Corvane at the inland assizes, past three Company checkpoints. The divers' matriarch, Sef, volunteers her oyster boat; a disgraced Company scribe, Ilsa, offers forgery skills. Emotional beat: fearful resolve—the family choosing danger together, Juniper insisting on coming despite Oren's objections.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the river toll, guards cross-check passengers against indenture rolls. Ilsa's forged papers nearly fail until Juniper—knowing the ledgers better than anyone—talks the clerk through his own filing errors. Emotional beat: Juniper discovering that the skills of their captivity are weapons, pride blooming through terror.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Burning Barge
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. A Company patrol torments a barge of divers as an intimidation tactic. Oren must decide whether to stay hidden or intervene, and chooses intervention, exposing them to pursuit. Emotional beat: the cost of solidarity—Oren wounded, the group now hunted, and Juniper furious and grateful in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Letters We Never Sent
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, night camp. Wounded and waiting out a patrol, Juniper finally reads all of their father's letters—apologies, stories, love. They write a reply they may never deliver. Emotional beat: grief and reconciliation, the realization that inheritance is memory carried forward, not property received.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Assizes Gate
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. The final gate: Company lawyers have reached the magistrate first, branding Oren a forger and Juniper an escaped indenture. Sef and the divers create a diversion at the docks; Ilsa presents the ledger's provenance chain. Emotional beat: desperate sacrifice, the family spending everything so Juniper can walk through that door.

chapters.title: Ledger and Lantern
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Before Magistrate Corvane, Juniper testifies as the last Dunmore, reading the ledger aloud by lantern light while Company clerks scramble. The audit collapses; estates are ordered restored. Elias's fate remains unknown, but Juniper lights a lantern for him on the harbor. Emotional beat: quiet triumph—history is no longer something that happens to other people; Juniper has become its keeper.
